Class 5 · Chapter 4 of 10

Tenths, hundredths and decimal calculations

Connect fractions and place value, then line up decimal places.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Fractions, mixed numbers and what is left. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can show decimals on a grid or line.
  • I can compare decimals and link them to fractions.
  • I can calculate decimal money and measures.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Tenths

Cut one whole into 10 equal parts. Each part is one tenth, 0.1.

3 tenths is 3/10, written 0.3.

The 3 sits in the tenths place.

Screen 2 of 5

Hundredths on a grid

A hundred-grid has 100 equal squares. Each is 0.01.

37 squares shaded is 37/100, or 0.37.

That is 3 tenths and 7 hundredths.

Screen 3 of 5

Tenths on a bar

Think of a bar split into 10 equal parts.

4 parts shaded is 0.4 or 4/10.

4/10 is the same as 2/5.

Screen 4 of 5

Line up the decimal points

When you add decimals, line up the points so tenths sit under tenths.

Add Rs 7.44 and Rs 26.56.

The total is Rs 34.00.

Screen 5 of 5

Compare decimals

Write both with the same number of places. 0.6 is 0.60.

Compare 60 hundredths with 45 hundredths.

0.6 is bigger than 0.45.

Words to know
tenth
One of ten equal parts. 0.1 is one tenth.
hundredth
One of one hundred equal parts. 0.01 is one hundredth.
decimal point
The dot that separates whole numbers from parts of a whole.

For parents

What your child learns

Decimals use place value beyond the ones place. A hundredths grid has 100 squares, so 25 shaded squares is 0.25. Facts about numbers must each be checked before you decide.

A common slip

Children often think a decimal with more digits is larger. Compare place by place from the left. For statements, test each one alone.

5-minute home activity: Hundred grid

  1. Draw a 10 by 10 grid on paper.
  2. Shade 25 squares and write the decimal.
  3. Shade 7 squares and write that decimal.
  4. Say which is bigger and why.
